display_name: Order an audited arrest of a canary's gauge
description: GAU-15 item 4 (2026-08-19). Orders a deliberate, bounded, audited freeze of one canary's context-gauge reporting, so the staleness detector can be exercised end to end instead of only against synthetic fixtures. The arrest withholds ONLY the canary's gauge write; its lifecycle clock keeps advancing through the normal reporting path, and that combination is what reproduces the real freeze signature -- a session still working while its gauge has stopped -- rather than an idle session, which the detector correctly ignores. A canary that went quiet on both clocks would test nothing. Nothing is injected downstream and nothing is special-cased in the store: the freeze is produced the same way production produces one. Every arrest is logged with who directed it, the exact window, and the alarm it expects, recorded BEFORE the outcome is known -- which is what makes any alarm mechanically attributable to a scheduled tamper rather than a real fault. An unattributable canary alarm does not merely fail to help; it trains stewards to discount the instrument, which is worse than having no canary at all. There is deliberately NO ambient test-mode environment variable: an env var leaves no audit trail, cannot be scoped to a window, and silently persists into runs nobody intended. Three refusals protect the attribution: a tamper may never target anything but a registered canary, the window must be bounded and forward-going (an arrest that never ends makes its alarms attributable forever, which is the same as not being attributable), and the expected alarm must be one the verifier can actually match, or the arrest would be unverifiable by construction.
embedding_description: Deliberately freezing a fake session's context reporting for a fixed, bounded period, recording who ordered the freeze and which alarm it should provoke, so the fleet's stopped-reporting monitoring can be proven to actually fire rather than only assumed to.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: agent_instance_id, directed_by, arrest_from, arrest_until, expected_notice_type, reason, recorded_at.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Quote the window and the expected alarm together, and name who directed it. Say clearly that any alarm arriving in this window for this canary is EXPECTED, so a reader who sees it in a channel does not treat it as an incident. Never describe the arrest as open-ended; the window's end is the point.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: The arrest proves nothing on its own -- judge it afterwards with verify_gauge_canary, once the window has CLOSED. A window still open has not had its chance, and reading it early says nothing either way.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: One canary-registration check plus one insert into the tamper audit log, through the state interface.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: not_a_canary: the target is not an active registered canary -- a tamper against a real session was refused, which is deliberate and not a bug. invalid_window: the arrest window was unreadable, empty, or backwards. invalid_expected_notice: the expected alarm is not one of gauge_stale_notice or gauge_coverage_notice. missing_directed_by: nobody was recorded as ordering the tamper. state_service_unavailable: the state service is not bound.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For not_a_canary, register the identity as a canary first -- never retarget the tamper at a real session to get past this. For invalid_window, supply both bounds as ISO-8601 with the end strictly after the start. For missing_directed_by, name the ordering role or session; the whole value of this log is that every arrest has an owner.
